'''Nomijinja''' (のみじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Nomimachi, {{ill|Takatsuki|en|Takatsuki|qid=Q335423|lt=Takatsuki City|1=Takatsuki}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} shrine, and its former Rank was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

== History ==
In the late 9th century, during the mid-{{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}} of {{ill|Emperor Uda|en|Emperor Uda|qid=Q349267|lt=Emperor Uda|1=Emperor Uda}} ({{ill|887|en|887|qid=Q25010|lt=887|1=887}} – {{ill|897|en|897|qid=Q30468|lt=897|1=897}}), an epidemic spread throughout the region. Following a divine oracle, {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozutennō|1=Gozu Tennō}} (identified with {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}) was enshrined, and as the epidemic subsided, a shrine building was constructed, establishing the Gozutennō Shrine.

In the late 10th century, when {{ill|Takatsuki Castle|ja|高槻城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takatsuki Castle|1=Takatsuki Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11670758}} was constructed, the shrine was venerated as a guardian of the castle.<ref name=nomijinja>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.nomijinja.jp/ |title=高槻城内守護 野見神社 |publisher=野見神社 |accessdate=2014-12-13}}</ref> However, in the 16th century when {{ill|Justo Takayama|en|Justo Takayama|qid=Q749873|lt=Takayama Ukon|1=Justo Takayama}} became the lord of Takatsuki Castle, his adherence to {{ill|Christianity|en|Christianity|qid=Q5043|lt=Christianity|1=Christianity}} led him to destroy the shrine building within the castle and confiscate its estate. Later, in the 5th year of the {{ill|Yuanhe|en|Yuanhe|qid=Q10889567|lt=Genna|1=Yuanhe}} era ({{ill|1619|en|1619|qid=Q6804|lt=1619|1=1619}}), the lord of Takatsuki Castle, {{ill|Matsudaira Ienobu|en|Matsudaira Ienobu|qid=Q5368670|lt=Matsudaira Ienobu|1=Matsudaira Ienobu}}, rebuilt the shrine building.<ref name=nomi_history>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.nomijinja.jp/%e5%be%a1%e7%94%b1%e7%b7%92-%e8%a1%8c%e4%ba%8b.html |title=野見神社 御由緒・年間行事 |publisher=野見神社 |accessdate=2014-12-13}}</ref>

In {{ill|1868|en|1868|qid=Q7717|lt=1868|1=1868}} (the first year of {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}), due to the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Separation of Shinto and Buddhism|1=Shinbutsu bunri}}, the name of the enshrined deity was changed to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, and furthermore, {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en|Nomi no Sukune|qid=Q965742|lt=Nomitatsune-no-Mikoto|1=Nomi no Sukune}} was enshrined alongside, prompting the shrine to be renamed “Nomijinja”. Consequently, although it is counted as one of the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} shrines listed in the {{ill|Engi Shiki Shinmei-chō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi Shiki Shinmei-chō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the publication “Historic Sites, Famous Landscapes, and Natural Monuments of Osaka Prefecture” asserts that the renaming to “Nomijinja”—by enshrining Nomitatsune to emulate a Shikinaisha—meant that its descendant shrine is the auxiliary shrine {{ill|Nomigami Shrine|ja|野身神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nomigami Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of {{ill|Kamigu Tenmangu|ja|上宮天満宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigu Tenmangu|1=Jōgū Tenmangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11358789}} in Takatsuki City.

In {{ill|1871|en|1871|qid=Q7746|lt=1871|1=1871}} (the 4th year of Meiji), it was classified as a prefectural shrine ({{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}) as a Shikinaisha; however, in November of the following year, {{ill|1872|en|1872|qid=Q7753|lt=1872|1=1872}} (the 5th year of Meiji), it was demoted to a village shrine ({{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}) for the reasons mentioned above.

== Enshrined Deities ==
* Main Deities – {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en|Nomi no Sukune|qid=Q965742|lt=Nomitatsune-no-Mikoto|1=Nomi no Sukune}}

== Shrine Grounds ==
=== Shrine Buildings ===
* Main Hall – Rebuilt in the 2nd year of {{ill|Tenna|en|Tenna|qid=Q1145289|lt=Tenwa|1=Tenna}} ({{ill|1682|en|1682|qid=Q7648|lt=1682|1=1682}}).
* Haiden – Renovated in {{ill|2003|en|2003|qid=Q1986|lt=2003|1=2003}} (the 15th year of {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}}).
* Noh Stage
* Shrine Office

=== Auxiliary Shrines ===
* {{ill|Nagai Shrine|ja|永井神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagai Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 野見神社 (高槻市)|1=Nomi Shrine (Q11646130)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11646130}} – Enshrined deity: the first lord of {{ill|Takatsuki Domain|en|Takatsuki Domain|qid=Q10863415|lt=Takatsuki Domain|1=Takatsuki Domain}}, {{ill|Nagai Naotoki|ja|永井直清|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagai Naotoki|1=Nagai Naokiyo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11549807}}. Founded in the 5th year of the {{ill|Kansei|en|Kansei|qid=Q1195131|lt=Kansei|1=Kansei}} era ({{ill|1793|en|1793|qid=Q7807|lt=1793|1=1793}}) by the 9th lord, {{ill|Nagai Naotoshi|ja|永井直進|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagai Naotoshi|1=Nagai Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11549817}}. Initially called “Naotoki Shrine”, it was referred to as “Naotoki Gongen” during the late Edo period. In the first year of the {{ill|Kaei|en|Kaei|qid=Q1146125|lt=Kaei|1=Kaei}} era ({{ill|1848|en|1848|qid=Q7647|lt=1848|1=1848}}), during the time of the 11th lord, {{ill|Nagai Naoteru|ja|永井直輝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagai Naoteru|1=Nagai Naoteru|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11549816}}, the main hall (a designated tangible cultural property of Takatsuki City) was restored, and the haiden (also a designated tangible cultural property) along with the karamon (quadrangular gate, designated tangible cultural property) were established. The karamon was repaired in {{ill|2010|en|2010|qid=Q1995|lt=2010|1=2010}} (the 22nd year of {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}}).  
: Annual Festival: April 24<ref name=nomi_setsumatsu>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.nomijinja.jp/%e6%91%82%e6%9c%ab%e7%a4%be.html |title=野見神社 - 摂末社 |publisher=野見神社 |accessdate=2014-12-13}}</ref>
* {{ill|Kojima Shrine|ja|小島神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kojima Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Enshrined deities: {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|市杵島姫命|lt=Ichikishima-hime-no-Mikoto|lt_ja=いちきしまひめのみこと|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime||1=Ichikishima-hime|2=fr|3=Ichikishimahime|4=ja|5=イチキシマヒメ|6=zh|7=市寸島比賣命|8=ru|9=Итикишима-химэ|10=de|11=Ichikishima-hime}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto|lt_ja=おほなむちのみこと|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}}, {{ill|Iwanagahime|ja|磐長姫命|lt=Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto|lt_ja=いわながひめのみこと|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwanagahime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イワナガヒメ|1=Iwanaga-hime|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8191705}}, and {{ill|Ameno Koyane|ja|天児屋根命|lt=Ameno Koyane-no-Mikoto|lt_ja=あめのこやねのみこと|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ameno Koyane|qid=Q2564508|1=Ame-no-Koyane|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2564508}}. Its founding date is unknown; the shrine building was newly constructed on October 1, {{ill|2021|en|2021|qid=Q49628|lt=2021|1=2021}} (the 3rd year of {{ill|Reiwa era|en|Reiwa era|qid=Q62609017|lt=Reiwa|1=Reiwa era}}).  
: Annual Festival: Second Sunday of October (Nomijinja Autumn Evening Festival)
* Shishamyojin – In the {{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|qid=Q329174|lt=Taishō period|1=Taishō era}} the separate shrines of Fukujinja, Inari Shrine, Iwajinsha, and Sorei Shrine were merged into one.  
: Annual Festival: April 11  
:: Fukujinja – Enshrined deities: {{ill|Shinatsuhikokami|ja|志那都比古神|lt=Shinatsuhikokami|lt_ja=しなつひこのかみ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinatsuhikokami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シナツヒコ|1=Shinatsuhiko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1073925}}, {{ill|Shinatsuhime|ja|志那都姫神|lt=Shinatsuhime|lt_ja=しなつひめのかみ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinatsuhime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Homusubi|ja|火産霊|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Homusubi|lt_ja=ほむすび|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Homusubi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}}, {{ill|Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|ja|金山比古神|lt=Kanayamahikokami|lt_ja=かなやまひこのかみ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 金山彦神}}, {{ill|Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|ja|金山姫神|lt=Kanayamahime|lt_ja=かなやまひめのかみ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 金山彦神}}, {{ill|Haniyamahikokami|ja|埴山比古神|lt=Haniyamahikokami|lt_ja=はにやまひこのかみ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniyamahikokami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (linked as {{ill|Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|en|Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|qid=Q9285919|lt=Haniyamas|1=Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime}} with display 埴山比古神), and {{ill|Mizuhanomenokami|ja|弥都波能売神|lt=Mizuhanomenokami|lt_ja=みづはのめのかみ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizuhanomenokami|qid=Q8191796|1=Mizuhanome|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8191796}}. Founded in August of the 9th year of {{ill|Kansei|en|Kansei|qid=Q1195131|lt=Kansei|1=Kansei}} ({{ill|1797|en|1797|qid=Q7820|lt=1797|1=1797}}) by {{ill|Nagai Naotoshi|ja|永井直進|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagai Naotoshi|1=Nagai Naonobu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11549817}}.  
:: Inari Shrine – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Ukanomitama|en|Ukanomitama|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukano Mitama-no-Kami|1=Ukanomitama}}. Founded in February of the 11th year of Kansei ({{ill|1799|en|1799|qid=Q7827|lt=1799|1=1799}}) by Nagai Naotoshi.  
:: Iwajinsha – Enshrined deities: (i) Yachimata Hikonami, (ii) Yachimata Hime, and (iii) Kunado-no-Kami. Founded in May of the 4th year of {{ill|Genbun|en|Genbun|qid=Q1145754|lt=Genbun|1=Genbun}} ({{ill|1739|en|1739|qid=Q7002|lt=1739|1=1739}}) by {{ill|Nagai Ryunosuke|ja|永井流之助|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagai Ryunosuke|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.  
:: Sorei Shrine – Enshrined are the successive chief priests, shrine priests, and parishioners who have devoted themselves to the shrine. Founded in {{ill|1878|en|1878|qid=Q7776|lt=1878|1=1878}} (the 11th year of {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}).
* {{ill|Takatsuki Ebisu Shrine|ja|高槻えびす神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takatsuki Ebisu Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Ebisu|ja|蛭子大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ebisu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to えびす}}. It was established in {{ill|1956|en|1956|qid=Q5221|lt=1956|1=1956}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Showa|1=Shōwa era}} 31) as a branch from {{ill|Nishinomiya Shrine|en|Nishinomiya Shrine|qid=Q705297|lt=Nishinomiya Shrine|1=Nishinomiya Shrine}}, and the current shrine building was constructed in {{ill|1966|en|1966|qid=Q2649|lt=1966|1=1966}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Showa|1=Shōwa era}} 41).  
: Takatsuki Ebisu Festival – January 10 (subdivided into the 9th: Evening Ebisu, 10th: Main Ebisu, 11th: Remaining Fortune)
* {{ill|Gokoku shrines|en|Gokoku shrines|qid=Q1534477|lt=Gokoku Shrine|1=Gokoku Shrines}} – Enshrined are the war dead of Takatsuki who perished in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|qid=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion|1=Satsuma Rebellion}}, {{ill|First Sino-Japanese War|en|First Sino-Japanese War|qid=Q178687|lt=First Sino-Japanese War|1=First Sino-Japanese War}}, {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|en|Russo-Japanese War|qid=Q159950|lt=Russo-Japanese War|1=Russo-Japanese War}}, {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|en|Second Sino-Japanese War|qid=Q170314|lt=Second Sino-Japanese War|1=Second Sino-Japanese War}}, and the {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|qid=Q184425|lt=Pacific War|1=Pacific War}}.  
: Annual Festival: Third Sunday of May<ref name=nomi_setsumatsu/>

* {{ill|Tondo Festival|ja|とんど|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tondo Festival|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 左義長|1=Sagichō Fire Festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q9332740}} – January 15

== Cultural Properties ==
=== Tangible Cultural Properties Designated by Takatsuki City ===
* Nagai Shrine buildings (main hall, haiden) with attached items: 4 ridge plaques and 1 Takatsuki Castle ema – Designated on June 14, {{ill|2005|en|2005|qid=Q2019|lt=2005|1=2005}} (Heisei 17).
* Nagai Shrine Karamon – Designated on June 14, 2005 (Heisei 17).
* Seventeen items of materials related to the traditional Nagai Naotoki of Nagai Shrine – Deposited at {{ill|Takatsuki City Shiroato Museum|ja|高槻市立しろあと歴史館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takatsuki City Shiroato Museum|1=Shiroato History Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11670762}}.
